result.rationale: The diff shows app/controllers/groups_controller.rb `members` uses `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` with no clamping — an uncapped limit would serialize the full membership and a huge offset forces a full walk/sort/discard. Unlike pre-diff code, this now publicly exposes arbitrary limit/offset to all callers (previously pagination was only honored for automatic groups). The mechanism is verifiable in the diff, but it is a robustness/DoS-hardening concern rather than a clear functional defect, so it fits important_non_bug.

judged_text: Uncapped limit/offset on the group members endpoint in app/controllers/groups_controller.rb allows any caller (including anonymous users on visible groups) to force full materialization/serialization of a group's entire membership via ?limit=999999999 or force Postgres to walk/sort and discard the entire member set via ?offset=1000000000; clamp both values (e.g., using Discourse's page_params helper) and reject non-positive values

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members`, the diff introduces client-controlled pagination for *all* groups: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i`, which are then passed directly into `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` and serialized. There is no clamping/validation of `limit` or `offset` (e.g., max page size, non-negative/non-zero), so a caller can request extremely large limits or offsets, potentially causing expensive DB work and large serialization responses. This was previously only applied to `automatic?` groups; the change expands the attack surface to all visible groups.
